intro: Novo Selo, a village near Veliko Tarnovo, keeps an oak in its centre that Bulgarian press reports put at about 500 years old, which would make it older than the village, founded in 1750. Nobody has published a measurement to settle it. The oak won Bulgaria's Tree with Roots contest in 2019 and was the country's entry to European Tree of the Year in 2020. It stands in the village centre and is free to see.
meta_description: The Venerable Oak of Novo Selo near Veliko Tarnovo, said to be about 500 years old, Bulgaria's entry to European Tree of the Year 2020.
question_answer: The tree we map in Novo Selo is the Venerable Oak, a pedunculate oak in the village centre that Bulgarian press reports put at about 500 years old. Nobody has published a measurement, so the age is a report rather than a count.
question_meta: The Venerable Oak of Novo Selo, said to be about 500 years old, stands in the village centre near Veliko Tarnovo. Where it is and what is known.
question_context: The village dates its founding to 1750, and the oak is said to be older, about 500 years by Bulgarian press reports citing specialists. Those two figures come from different places and should be kept apart: the founding date is the village's own history, the age is a report, and no girth, height or ring count has been published to test it. What the record does show is how much the village thinks of it. The contest entry calls it a pedunculate oak, and the village treats it as the keeper of its history since 1750. In December 2019 it won Bulgaria's Tree with Roots contest with 1,073 votes, and in 2020 it represented Bulgaria in European Tree of the Year. An arborist's assessment was promised at the time, and we have found no report of it since. It stands in the centre of the village, free to see, and the trip from Veliko Tarnovo is best made by car. If you know its girth, tell us.

trees.story:
The village of Novo Selo, near Veliko Tarnovo, dates its founding to 1750. The oak in its centre is said to be about 500 years old, which would make the tree older than the village by a couple of centuries.

Those two numbers do not come from the same place, and it is worth keeping them apart. The founding date is the village's own history. The 500 years comes from Bulgarian press reports citing specialists, and nobody has published a measurement, a ring count, a girth or a height. So the honest version is simpler: a big old oak that the village regards as the keeper of its history since 1750, of an age nobody has settled. If you know more, tell us.

It stands in the middle of the village, a landmark rather than a secret. In December 2019 it won Bulgaria's Tree with Roots contest with 1,073 votes, and in 2020 it was the country's entry to European Tree of the Year. At the time an arborist's assessment was promised, and we have found no report of it since.

The contest entry names it as a pedunculate oak; the press says only oak.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the big old oak at the heart of Novo Selo, the tree the village treats as its landmark. It stands in the village centre.
